When you play Taste of Vitae, does it count only the blood lost
during the current strike resolution phase? Or does it count
blood lost for the entire round (or the portion of the round
after a previous Taste, if played)?

resolution, but I read something last week that made me wonder...

> When you play Taste of Vitae, does it count only the blood lost

> after a previous Taste, if played)?
> I used to think it would only count for the current strike

Card Title: Taste of Vitae
Card Text: Only usable after strike resolution. This vampire gains
an amount of blood equal to the amount lost by the
opposing vampire during this round of combat. Not
usable by a vampire going into torpor.

The entire round. For example, if Basilia (5/10) and Javier Montoya (0/10)
go to combat. Basilia plays Drawing Out the Beast and Javier plays Theft
of Vitae. Javier would gain 2 blood from the Theft and then would lose 1
each from Basilia's punch and DotB. So...if Basilia played Taste of Vitae,
she would gain 2 blood to fill back to the 5 blood she started the combat
with.

Correct, LSJ? Or will the damage from DotB happen after the opportunity
to play Taste of Vitae has passed?

Well, Basilia's hand damage is aggravated, so let's pretend Javier had
previously played Seeds of Corruption on Basilia (cancelling her
aggravated-damage-special).

So Javier strikes: Theft (superior) and Basilia strikes: hands (for 1).
Javier gains two blood and takes one damage while Basilia loses two blood.
Javier: 2/10 Basilia: 3/10 Then Javier burns one blood to heal the damage.
Javier: 1/10 Basilia: 3/10 Then, after strike resolution, Basilia plays
Taste to gain the one Javier lost. Javier: 1/10 Basilia: 4/10

At the end of the round (after the opportunity to press, etc.), Javier takes
one damage from DotB.
Javier: 0/10 Basilia: 4/10

Messages.Author: John M. Baker
Messages.Body:
Dharzhak wrote:
>
>Card Title: Taste of Vitae
>Card Text: Only usable after strike resolution. This vampire gains
> an amount of blood equal to the amount lost by the
> opposing vampire during this round of combat. Not
> usable by a vampire going into torpor.
>
>The entire round. For example, if Basilia (5/10) and Javier Montoya (0/10)
>go to combat. Basilia plays Drawing Out the Beast and Javier plays Theft
>of Vitae. Javier would gain 2 blood from the Theft and then would lose 1
>each from Basilia's punch and DotB. So...if Basilia played Taste of Vitae,
>she would gain 2 blood to fill back to the 5 blood she started the combat
>with.
>

IANALSJ.
Uh, read the card text. No. Firstly, you can't play Taste after DotB does
its
damage (see LSJ). Secondly, Taste only count BLOOD lost, not total damage
taken. Let's go back to the previous example, and say that Basilia does
aggravated hand damage. Javier Thefts 2 blood, then takes 1 aggravated.
Javier can't heal the aggravated, and so he goes to torpor with 2 blood.
Notice that Javier at no time in the round lost any blood. So, Taste will
net Basilia no blood in this case.

As another example, let's say that we've got Navar MacLaren with 0/1 blood,
and he's fighting Lazverinus with a Crimson Sentinel with 12 soul counters.
Navar strikes for 1 damage, Lazzy is nice and only strikes for 15. Lazzy
plays
Taste. How much blood does Lazzy get before the excess drains off? None.
Why? Navar never lost blood, despite taking 15 damage.

John Baker
